tags.name: Eligibility
tags.description: Eligibility API will enable Visa Direct Connect clients to check eligibility of recipient payment instrument(Cards). It will provide the details if the card can be used for payout/payin, cardis fast funds enabled and what other non-visa networks are enabled.

tags.name: Exception Management
tags.description: This API allows an Originating Entity to cancel, reverse or adjust the original transaction for a Card, Accounts or wallet payout/payin transaction. This API is used by Originator after the original payout/payin transaction is successfully received by Visa Direct Connect.

tags.name: Payin
tags.description: Payin API will enable originators to pull money from a card.

tags.name: Transaction Management
tags.description: Originators can get the transaction details after the cards/account/wallet payout/payin transactions are received or transactions went through some post transaction operations like payment delivered, cancelled, rejected or adjusted.

tags.name: Validate
tags.description: This API allows an Originating Entity to validate the payload for a Accounts or wallet payout before sending in the actual payout request for processing, thus ensuring greater probability of success and allowing for a more seamless transaction flow. The ISO field names provided are provided by Visa for guidance only. Clients are advised to check the ISO field mappings themselves.

metadataVersion.description:
This is the version of the updated route definition. 
It is in the format <major-version>.<minor-version>.<patch>.

* patch updates are documentation updates only and should not influence the processing of a payout transaction. Example: changes to the description of Purpose of Payment code.

* minor-version updates indicate backward compatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Example: addition of a new Purpose of Payment code.

* major-version updates indicate backward incompatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Such changes are usually regulatory in nature or due to partner migration on Visa's backend. Example: Purpose of Payment code changing from a "conditional"/ "recommended" to a "required" field.

Originators may choose to specify any or all of the following optional parameters to receive as part of the API response.

E.g. Originators may specify comma-separated, optional parameters such as optionalResponseParameters (motoECIIndicator), if they want to receive motoECIIndicator in the API response.

motoECIIndicator: Identifies the level of security used in an electronic commerce transaction over an open network (for example, the Internet) or the type of mail or telephone order. Acquirers supply indicator values, which V.I.P. forwards in requests and advices to issuers that have successfully tested to receive them. The subfield is dropped if issuers have not successfully completed testing or choose not to receive it.

metadataVersion.description:
This is the version of the updated route definition. 
It is in the format <major-version>.<minor-version>.<patch>.

* patch updates are documentation updates only and should not influence the processing of a payout transaction. Example: changes to the description of Purpose of Payment code.

* minor-version updates indicate backward compatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Example: addition of a new Purpose of Payment code.

* major-version updates indicate backward incompatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Such changes are usually regulatory in nature or due to partner migration on Visa's backend. Example: Purpose of Payment code changing from a "conditional"/ "recommended" to a "required" field.

- Money transfer: AA, PP, BI, FT, WT;

metadataVersion.description:
This is the version of the updated route definition. 
It is in the format <major-version>.<minor-version>.<patch>.

* patch updates are documentation updates only and should not influence the processing of a payout transaction. Example: changes to the description of Purpose of Payment code.

* minor-version updates indicate backward compatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Example: addition of a new Purpose of Payment code.

* major-version updates indicate backward incompatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Such changes are usually regulatory in nature or due to partner migration on Visa's backend. Example: Purpose of Payment code changing from a "conditional"/ "recommended" to a "required" field.

destinationAmount.description:
The destination amount that will be deposited to the beneficiary account, expressed in the Recipient bank currency code provided in the original request. If the Originating Entity sends a payout in a currency that is not the same as the destination currency then Visa will perform FX conversion and calculate the amount to be deposited to the beneficiary bank account, and provide this information back to the Originating Entity.

Note: Destination amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Payouts Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units.

ageVerificationRequestDetails.description:
Echoes back the age thresholds exactly as submitted in the request ageVerification field.
Use this field to map each position in ageVerificationResults to its corresponding age threshold,
since results are returned in the same order as the thresholds provided.
For example, if this field returns 18D30D50D and ageVerificationResults is VVI, the cardholder
satisfies the 18+ and 30+ thresholds but not 50+.

scaEnvironmentOutageIndicator.description:

Valid Values :
FALSE - No authentication outage
TRUE - Authentication outage

If this exemption does not apply to the transaction, the value of "FALSE" is optional and the field may be omitted entirely.This field maps to ISO8583 Field 34 – Dataset ID 02 -Tag 87.

delegatedAuthenticationIndicator.description:
Delegated Authentication Indicator.

Valid Values :
FALSE - Delegated authentication not claimed/requested
TRUE - Delegated authentication claimed/requested

If this exemption does not apply to the transaction, the value of "FALSE" is optional and the field may be omitted entirely.
Clients requesting this exemption should also provide the the following request parameters:
1. visaMerchantIdentifier value, which is an unique identifier assigned by Visa for each merchant included in the identification program.Issuers can obtain a list of Visa-assigned merchant identifiers from Visa Online (VOL).
2. Cardholder Authentication Verification Value (CAVV) OR Token Authentication Verification Value (TAVV)

Program Qualification: Acquirers that choose to participate will identify and qualify potential Delegates that meet the qualification criteria and work with them to evidence how their authentication capabilities are compliant and to obtain their agreement to the requirements of the Program through the Readiness Questionnaire. Token requestors may submit their Readiness Questionnaire directly to Visa. On a per transaction basis, the delegated entity will flag to the Issuer that SCA was performed through EMV 3DS (2.2 only) or VTS.

This field maps to ISO8583->TLV Field 34, Dataset ID 4A, Tag 8A.

trustedMerchantExemptionIndicator.description:

If this exemption does not apply to the transaction, the value of "FALSE" is optional and the field may be omitted entirely.

CurrencyInfoReason.description:
The reason denotes why a particular currency change has happened.
1. FLEXIBLE_SETTLEMENT_DISABLED – The flexible settlement is disabled for the client. This applies only when the currentStatus is DISABLED. 
2. CURRENCY_DISABLED - The currency is disabled for the client. This applies only when the currentStatus is DISABLED.
3. FREEZE_MANUAL – The currency has been manually frozen. This applies only when the currentStatus is DISABLED.
4. FREEZE_SETTLEMENT_DUE - The currency is automatically frozen following a settlement breach and will stay frozen until the outstanding amount is paid. This applies only when the currentStatus is DISABLED.
5. FREEZE_ALL_FREEZE_ENABLED - This currency is frozen because another currency is overdue, and the all-freeze setting is enabled. This applies only when the currentStatus is DISABLED.
6. UNFREEZE_MANUAL - The currency has been manually enabled temporarily. This applies only when the currentStatus is ENABLED.
7. NO_DUES - The currency is enabled and can be used to send payouts. This applies only when the currentStatus is ENABLED.

groupName.description:
The name of the metadata element/enum.
This generic Identity Group object can represent either 'Recipient Identity Field Group object' or 'Bank Account Registration Field Group object' . 
Enum value signifies the particular metadata element. 

For example : 
 a) if enum is "address", this can contain array of 'IdentityField' object where each object can represent elements like addressLine1, addressLine2, city, countryCode, postalCode etc    

 b) enum can be "identificationList", which contains array of "IdentityField' objects, one of the IdentityField object can have elementName="idType" and inputType="list", in this scenario array of IdentityListItem will have 
 [
   {
     "label": "Passport",
     "value": "Passport"
   },
   {
     "label": "National ID Card",
     "value": "National ID Card"
   },
   {
     "label": "Driving License",
     "value": "Driving License"
   }
 ], 
 second 'IdentityField' Object -> elementName as "identificationNumber" with inputType="text" 
 third 'IdentityField' Object -> elementName as "identificationCountry" with inputType="text" 
 fourth 'IdentityField' Object -> elementName as "validFromDate" with inputType="text"
 fifth  'IdentityField' Object -> elementName as "validToDate" with inputType="text" and so on.

 c) If enum is "additionalData",this will have array of two 'IdentityField' objects, one representing 'additionalDataKey' and other one 'additionalDataValue'.

 d) If enum is "name", "middleName" may be required for some countries (e.g. Africa). This can be accommodated by appending a space and then middleName to <firstName>

metadataVersion.description:
This is the version of the route definition recalled by VISA. 
It is in the format <major-version>.<minor-version>.<patch>.

* patch updates are documentation updates only and should not influence the processing of a payout transaction. Example: changes to the description of Purpose of Payment code.

* minor-version updates indicate backward compatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Example: addition of a new Purpose of Payment code.

* major-version updates indicate backward incompatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Such changes are usually regulatory in nature or due to partner migration on Visa's backend. Example: Purpose of Payment code changing from a "conditional"/ "recommended" to a "required" field.

destinationAmount.description:
The destination amount that will be deposited to the recipient account, expressed in the Recipient bank currency code provided in the original request. If the Originating Entity sends a payout in a currency that is not the same as the destination currency then Visa will perform FX conversion and calculate the amount to be deposited to the recipient bank account, and provide this information back to the Originating Entity.

Note: Destination amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Visa Direct Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units.

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JPY is 0. If the amount is JPY 10,000, then this field should populate “10000”.

name.description:
masterCardPartnerIdCode

Conditional.

This field identifies a specific partnership agreement, generally between specific acceptors and issuers. may be used for transactions on accounts issued under co-branding agreements when one of the co-branding partners originates the transaction.

This field is conditionally required for all MasterCard transactions.

masterCardIndependentSalesOrganizationId

Conditional.

This field contains the "Company ID" that is assigned during the time of registration with Mastercard Connect as a service provider and must be provided by the acquirer.

This field is conditionally required for all MasterCard transactions.

masterCardSubMerchantId

Sub-Merchant ID containing the sponsored merchant ID. This field is conditionally required when a payment facilitator is involved and for all MasterCard transactions.

masterCardMerchantPaymentGatewayId

This field contains merchant payment gateway ID assigned by Mastercard, provided by the acquirer when a registered merchant payment gateway service provider participates in the transaction. Value is right-justified and zero-filled.

merchantPseudoAbaNumber

This is a number that uniquely identifies the originator when they sign up to send Push Payment Gateway transactions. On enrollment, an originator will get a single pseudo-value that is assigned by Visa. The other networks will assign their own unique values for the originator.

Note:
Supported only in US for domestic transactions involving Push Payments Gateway Service.

destinationAmount.description:
The destination amount that will be deposited to the beneficiary account, expressed in the destination currency code provided in the original request. If the Originating Entity sends a payout in a currency that is not the same as the destination currency then Visa will perform FX conversion and calculate the amount to be deposited to the beneficiary bank account, and provide this information back to the Originating Entity.

Note: Transaction amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Payouts Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units. 

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JPY is 0. If the amount is JPY 10,000, then this field should populate “10000”.

name.description:
masterCardPartnerIdCode

Conditional.

This field identifies a specific partnership agreement, generally between specific acceptors and issuers. may be used for transactions on accounts issued under co-branding agreements when one of the co-branding partners originates the transaction.

This field is conditionally required for all MasterCard transactions.

masterCardIndependentSalesOrganizationId

Conditional.

This field contains the "Company ID" that is assigned during the time of registration with Mastercard Connect as a service provider and must be provided by the acquirer.

This field is conditionally required for all MasterCard transactions.

masterCardSubMerchantId

Sub-Merchant ID containing the sponsored merchant ID. This field is conditionally required when a payment facilitator is involved and for all MasterCard transactions.

masterCardMerchantPaymentGatewayId

This field contains merchant payment gateway ID assigned by Mastercard, provided by the acquirer when a registered merchant payment gateway service provider participates in the transaction. Value is right-justified and zero-filled.

merchantPseudoAbaNumber

This is a number that uniquely identifies the originator when they sign up to send Push Payment Gateway transactions. On enrollment, an originator will get a single pseudo-value that is assigned by Visa. The other networks will assign their own unique values for the originator.

Note:
Supported only in US for domestic transactions involving Push Payments Gateway Service.

verificationStatus.description:
Provides the status of verification request.
* COMPLETED - Request was completed and result is available.
* NOT_COMPLETED - Service Provider not available.

List of currency codes accepted by the specific requested account which is verified by the Account verification services.

bankAccountName.description: Field to indicate the actual name of the accountholder (if provided by account verification service provider).

accountIdentifierMatch.description:
Indicates if the account identifier provided matches the recipient's bank account identifier found.
- YES: Match
- NO: No Match

CurrencyInfoReason-1.description:
The reason denotes why a particular currency change has happened.
1. FLEXIBLE_SETTLEMENT_DISABLED – The flexible settlement is disabled for the client. This applies only when the currentStatus is DISABLED. 
2. CURRENCY_DISABLED - The currency is disabled for the client. This applies only when the currentStatus is DISABLED.
3. FREEZE_MANUAL – The currency has been manually frozen. This applies only when the currentStatus is DISABLED.
4. FREEZE_SETTLEMENT_DUE - The currency is automatically frozen following a settlement breach and will stay frozen until the outstanding amount is paid. This applies only when the currentStatus is DISABLED.
5. FREEZE_ALL_FREEZE_ENABLED - This currency is frozen because another currency is overdue, and the all-freeze setting is enabled. This applies only when the currentStatus is DISABLED.
6. UNFREEZE_MANUAL - The currency has been manually enabled temporarily. This applies only when the currentStatus is ENABLED.
7. NO_DUES - The currency is enabled and can be used to send payouts. This applies only when the currentStatus is ENABLED.

destinationAmount.description:
The destination amount that will be deposited to the recipient account, expressed in the Recipient bank currency code provided in the original request. If the Originating Entity sends a payout in a currency that is not the same as the destination currency then Visa will perform FX conversion and calculate the amount to be deposited to the recipient bank account, and provide this information back to the Originating Entity.

Note: Destination amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Visa Direct Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units.

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JPY is 0. If the amount is JPY 10,000, then this field should populate “10000”.

approvedAmount.description:
This field contains the partially approved AFT transaction amount in the currency specified by the currency code in 'transactionCurrencyCode'. 
The amount of POS funds requested by the cardholder, expressed in the local currency in an original authorization or financial transaction. 
This field also contains the acquirer-assessed surcharge.            

Note: Transaction amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Payouts Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units. 

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JPY is 0. If the amount is JPY 10,000, then this field should populate “10000”.

ISO20022 field name: Instructed Amount

retrievalReferenceNumber.description:
This is a unique identifier generated by Visa for a card transaction

The format is ydddhhnnnnnn
yddd - The first four digits must be a valid Julian date format, where the first digit = 0-9 (last digit of current year) and the next three digits = 001-366 (number of the day in the year). 
hh - can be the two digit hour in a 24 hour clock (00-23) during which the transaction is performed. 
nnnnnn - can be the systemsTraceAuditNumber or any 6 digit number

settlementConversionRate.description:

Note:
Supported only in US for domestic transactions involving Push Payments Gateway Service.

destinationAmount.description:
The destination amount that will be deposited to the recipient account, expressed in the Recipient bank currency code provided in the original request. If the Originating Entity sends a payout in a currency that is not the same as the destination currency then Visa will perform FX conversion and calculate the amount to be deposited to the recipient bank account, and provide this information back to the Originating Entity.

Note: Destination amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Visa Direct Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units.

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JPY is 0. If the amount is JPY 10,000, then this field should populate “10000”.

ISO20022 field name: Instructed Amount

cardAcceptorId.description: An identifier that uniquely identifies the Originating Entity.  For Push to Card transactions, Card Acceptor Terminal ID (CAID) should be populated

transactionAmount.description:
This field contains the transaction amount in the currency specified by the currency code in 'transactionCurrencyCode'. 
The amount of POS funds requested by the cardholder, expressed in the local currency in an original authorization or financial transaction. 
This field also contains the acquirer-assessed surcharge.            

Note: Transaction amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Payouts Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units. 

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JPY is 0. If the amount is JPY 10,000, then this field should populate “10000”.

ISO20022 field name: Instructed Amount

originalActionCode.description: Contains a code that provides the result of original payout request when current request is identified as duplicate of original and actionCode will be 94.

transmissionDateTime.description: The time the request was processed by Visa

systemTraceAuditNumber.description: This field contains a number generated by Visa that uniquely identifies a transaction and all message types. The trace number is a key data element used to match a response to its request or to match a message to others for a given transaction set

transactionCurrencyCode.description:
The 3-character ISO-4217 code in this field reflects the currency associated to the transaction amount. 

Format: 3-character ISO-4217 (Alpha-3) currency code

Example: "PHP"

retrievalReferenceNumber.description:
This is a unique identifier generated by Visa for a card transaction

The format is ydddhhnnnnnn
yddd - The first four digits must be a valid Julian date format, where the first digit = 0-9 (last digit of current year) and the next three digits = 001-366 (number of the day in the year). 
hh - can be the two digit hour in a 24 hour clock (00-23) during which the transaction is performed. 
nnnnnn - can be the systemsTraceAuditNumber or any 6 digit number

responseReasonCode.description: This field contains the merchant advice code value received from Mastercard authorization response messages.

transactionLinkIdentifier.description: Transaction Link Identifier returned from other networks like MasterCard and Pulse

mastercardElectronicCommerceIndicators.description: This field contains the security-level indicator for Mastercard issuer-authenticated transactions.

last4ofPAN.description: This field contains the last four digits of the cardholder primary account number (PAN).            This field is returned only when token is provided in the payout request.

approvalCode.description:
This is a unique authorization code for an approved transaction from Issuer

title.description: The title indicating the country of the metadata response

version.description:
This is the version of the metadata response. 
It is in the format \<major-version-number\>.\<minor-version-number\>.\<minor-sub-version-number\>.

* minor-sub-version-number updates are documentation updates only and should not influence the processing of a payout transaction. Example: changes to the description of Purpose of Payment code.

* minor-version-number updates indicate backward compatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Example: addition of a new Purpose of Payment code.

* major-version-number updates indicate backward incompatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Such changes are usually regulatory in nature or due to partner migration on Visa's backend. Example: Purpose of Payment code changing from a "recommended" to a "required" field.

AccountNumber.description: When present, this field contains recipient’s account number or alias at the bank.

amount.description: This is the amount of money remitted for the referred document. Note that this field accepts signed amounts. A positive amount value indicates amounts flowing in the direction of the payout transaction, and due to the recipient . A negative amount value indicates the amount due back to the sender, i.e. a reduction in the total remitted amount. An amount value without the explicit mention of sign would be assumed positive.

- PAYMENT_RETURNED: Visa has reverted the card payout instruction, fund is not moved
- PAYMENT_ERROR: Visa encountered error when processing the card payout instruction, fund is in unknown state

retrievalReferenceNumber.description:
This is a unique identifier generated by Visa for a card transaction

The format is ydddhhnnnnnn
yddd - The first four digits must be a valid Julian date format, where the first digit = 0-9 (last digit of current year) and the next three digits = 001-366 (number of the day in the year). 
hh - can be the two digit hour in a 24 hour clock (00-23) during which the transaction is performed. 
nnnnnn - can be the systemsTraceAuditNumber or any 6 digit number

exemptionReasonCode.description:

8A02 = Issuer not participating in Visa Delegated Authentication Program
8A04 = Indeterminate or invalid issuer response

8A08 = CAVV invalid value
8A76 = Did not meet delegation criteria (Issuer supplied)
8473 = Cardholder has not trusted the merchant (issuer supplied)
8474 = Did not meet the exemption criteria (issuer supplied)

settlementAmount.description: This is the amount to be debited from Originating Entity/Visa Client's funding account.

destinationAmount.description:
The destination amount that will be deposited to the recipient account, expressed in the destination currency code provided in the original request. If the Originating Entity sends a payout in a currency that is not the same as the destination currency then Visa will perform FX conversion and calculate the amount to be deposited to the recipient bank account, and provide this information back to the Originating Entity.

Note: Transaction amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Visa Direct Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units. 

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JPY is 0. If the amount is JPY 10,000, then this field should populate “10000”.

ISO20022 field name: Transaction Information And Status - Remitted Amount

transactionAmount.description:

Note: Transaction amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Visa Direct Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units.

ISO20022 field name: Instructed Amount

This is an optional field, and it can indicate a change in the expected posting date.

ISO20022 field name: Interbank Settlement Date

transactionCurrencyCode.description:

• Use a 3-digit numeric or 3-character alpha ISO currency code for currency of the sender.

Adjust amount accordingly based on chosen transactionCurrencyCode.

If the Originating Entity sends a payout in a currency that is not the same as the destination currency then Visa will perform FX conversion and calculate the amount to be deposited to the recipient bank account, and provide this information back to the Originating Entity.

Note: Transaction amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Visa Direct Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units. 

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JPY is 0. If the amount is JPY 10,000, then this field should populate “10000”.

ISO20022 field name: Transaction Information And Status - Remitted Amount

transactionAmount.description:
The amount to debit from merchant's funding account or credit to recipient's bank account.

Note: Transaction amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Visa Direct Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units. 

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JPY is 0. If the amount is JPY 10,000, then this field should populate “10000”.

ISO20022 field name: Instructed Amount

Example: GBP

panEntryMode.description:
Required for Card Present Transfer

A 2-digit code that identifies the method used to enter the cardholder account number and card expiration date. This code specifies whether the entire magnetic stripe is included in an authorization or financial request.

Recommended value for card/token verification for Card not present transactions is 01. Default value is 01.

Refer to PAN Entry Mode Codes (https://developer.visa.com/request_response_codes#pan_entry_mode_codes)

motoECIIndicator.description:
Identifies the level of security used in an electronic commerce transaction over an open network (for example, the Internet) or the type of mail or telephone order. Acquirers supply indicator values, which Visa forwards in requests and advices to issuers that have successfully tested to receive them. The subfield is dropped if issuers have not successfully completed testing or choose not to receive it.
If not provided, Visa will default its value to 7

posConditionCode.description:
Required for Card Present Transfer

Contains a code identifying transaction conditions at the point of sale or point of service. For messages that follow an original request, this code identifies the type of processing being done.

Recommended value for Address/cvv2/account verification without authorization is 59. Default value is 59.

Refer to POS Condition Codes (https://developer.visa.com/request_response_codes#pos_cond_code_codes)

specialConditionIndicatorMerchant.description: Cryptocurrency indicator with the value of “7” can be used to identify the purchase of cryptocurrency, thereby providing greater visibility to the issuers.

PointOfServiceData.description: Conditional Required for Card Present Transfer Contains a code identifying transaction conditions at the point-of-sale or point of service. For messages that follow an original request, this code identifies the type of processing being done. Note: For a CardPresent or Token Transactions, this field is required. If this Object is not passed in the request then API will default at following values: "pointOfServiceData": { "panEntryMode": "01","posConditionCode": "59","motoECIIndicator":"7"}"

metadataVersion.description:
This is the version of the updated route definition. 
It is in the format <major-version>.<minor-version>.<patch>.

* patch updates are documentation updates only and should not influence the processing of a payout transaction. Example: changes to the description of Purpose of Payment code.

* minor-version updates indicate backward compatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Example: addition of a new Purpose of Payment code.

* major-version updates indicate backward incompatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Such changes are usually regulatory in nature or due to partner migration on Visa's backend. Example: Purpose of Payment code changing from a "conditional"/ "recommended" to a "required" field.

status.description:
Status of the transaction - PAYMENT_RECEIVED: Visa has acknowledged the payout instruction has been received. This event can be repeated when 'fundingStatus' or 'expectedPostingDate' fields change value - AWAITING_INFORMATION: More information required by Visa before transaction can be processed. - PAYMENT_SENT: The payout has been submitted to the Network partner by PSP. This event can be repeated 'fundingStatus' or 'expectedPostingDate' fields change value - PAYMENT_DELIVERED: The payout has been posted to the recipient's account. This status is applicable for all Wallet Payments and Account Payments only when provided by the Network Partner. - DELIVERED_TO_SCHEME: The payout has been submitted to the local country scheme for further processing. This status is applicable for Account Payments only when provided by the Network Partner. - DELIVERED_TO_RECIPIENT_BANK: The payout has been submitted to the recipient’s bank. This status is applicable for Account Payments only when provided by the Network Partner.

UCAFField.description: This field contains Mastercard e-commerce Universal Cardholder Authentication data in encrypted form. It may also contain Mastercard telephone order data.

UCAFCollectionIndicator.description: E-commerce indicator that Mastercard Universal Cardholder Authentication data is included in the message.

transactionLinkIdentifier.description: Transaction Link Identifier returned from other networks like MasterCard and Pulse

secureRemoteTokenCryptogram.description: This field contains Mastercard digital payment/Cryptogram data associated with the token.

remoteCommerceAcceptorIdentifier.description: This field contains a merchant identifier encoded as Base64. For example website URL or reverse domain name.

payoutId.description: For a Push transaction the identifier of Pull transaction that funds it can be provided, to associate the Pull and Push transactions

surcharge.description:
When present, this field contains surcharge as assessed by the Originating Entity. Values in this field must be included in the transactionAmount and should be in the same currency and format as defined in the transactionAmount field.

Note: if card credential is provided in senderDetail, fund is debited by transactionAmount from sender's card; but credited by transactionAmount - surcharge to recipient's card
Technical Specifications - Appendix E Country and Currency codes for VDC.

sencondaryId.description: secondaryId is used for C2B use case in the CEMEA region where payee initiates the OCT to the payer. The merchant or acquirer may use this field to obtain an Agreement Id in order to process the request.

motoECIIndicator.description:
Identifies the level of security used in an electronic commerce transaction over an open network (for example, the Internet) or the type of mail or telephone order. Acquirers supply indicator values, which Visa forwards in requests and advices to issuers that have successfully tested to receive them. The subfield is dropped if issuers have not successfully completed testing or choose not to receive it.
If not provided, Visa will default its value to 7 for US and 5 for rest of the world, for e-Commerce transaction

purposeOfPayment.description:
Purpose of payment code is required in certain markets to clearly identify the purpose of the payment based on the standard values defined for respective market

Conditional (Refer to Payouts Endpoint Guide on country-specific required fields and lengths)

ISO20022 field name: Purpose of Payment

messageReasonCode.description:
Conditional.

Contains codes that combined with some other fields such as the BAI (Business Application Id) identify some unique use cases. For Sales Tax rebates this field should be populated with the value 5120 (Value-added tax/Sales Tax) along with the businessApplicationId field set to the value 'FD' which indicates this push funds transfer is being conducted in order to facilitate a sales tax refund.

transactionAmount.description:
This field contains the transaction amount in the currency specified by the currency code in 'transactionCurrencyCode'. 
The amount of POS funds requested by the cardholder, expressed in the local currency in an original authorization or financial transaction. 
This field also contains the acquirer-assessed surcharge.            

Note: Transaction amount should be numeric. Refer to the Payouts Endpoint Guide on country-specific currency minor units. Refer to SMS POS Visa & Visa Electron
Technical Specifications - Appendix E Country and Currency codes for Card.

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JOD is 3, the amount is JOD 100.996.

feeProgramIndicator.description: Note: If present, a valid value is required. Spaces or special characters are not allowed.

businessApplicationId.description:
Business Application Identifier (BAI) identifies the type of program for which the payment is being sent, i.e. whether it is a funds disbursement, money transfer etc. It should be a valid value allowed by Visa and approved for the program during onboarding.

Valid BAI for Push to Cards:
- Money transfer: AA, PP, BI, FT, WT; 
- Non-money transfer: BB, BP, CP, FD, GD, GP, LO, MD, OG, PD, PS

- PAYMENT_DELIVERED: The payout has been posted to the recipient's account. This status is only applicable for Wallet Payments

status.description:
Status of the transaction - PAYMENT_RECEIVED: Visa has acknowledged the payout instruction has been received. This event can be repeated when 'fundingStatus' or 'expectedPostingDate' fields change value - AWAITING_INFORMATION: More information required by Visa before transaction can be processed. - PAYMENT_SENT: The payout has been submitted to the Network partner by PSP. This event can be repeated if 'fundingStatus' or 'expectedPostingDate' fields change value. - PAYMENT_DELIVERED: The payout has been posted to the recipient's account. This status is applicable for all Wallet Payments and Account Payments only when provided by the Network Partner. - DELIVERED_TO_SCHEME: The payout has been submitted to the local country scheme for further processing. This status is applicable for Account Payments only when provided by the Network Partner. - DELIVERED_TO_RECIPIENT_BANK: The payout has been submitted to the recipient’s bank. This status is applicable for Account Payments only when provided by the Network Partner.

surcharge.description:
When present, this field contains surcharge as assessed by the Originating Entity. Values in this field must be included in the transactionAmount and should be in the same currency and format as defined in the transactionAmount field.

Note: if card credential is provided in senderDetail, fund is debited by transactionAmount from sender's card; but credited by transactionAmount - surcharge to recipient's card
Technical Specifications - Appendix E Country and Currency codes for VDC.

sencondaryId.description: secondaryId is used for C2B use case in the CEMEA region where payee initiates the OCT to the payer. The merchant or acquirer may use this field to obtain an Agreement Id in order to process the request.

motoECIIndicator.description:
Identifies the level of security used in an electronic commerce transaction over an open network (for example, the Internet) or the type of mail or telephone order. Acquirers supply indicator values, which Visa forwards in requests and advices to issuers that have successfully tested to receive them. The subfield is dropped if issuers have not successfully completed testing or choose not to receive it.
If not provided, Visa will default its value to 7 for US and 5 for rest of the world, for e-Commerce transaction

purposeOfPayment.description:
Purpose of payment code is required in certain markets to clearly identify the purpose of the payment based on the standard values defined for respective market

Conditional (Refer to Payouts Endpoint Guide on country-specific required fields and lengths)

ISO20022 field name: Purpose of Payment

messageReasonCode.description:
Conditional.

Contains codes that combined with some other fields such as the BAI (Business Application Id) identify some unique use cases. For Sales Tax rebates this field should be populated with the value 5120 (Value-added tax/Sales Tax) along with the businessApplicationId field set to the value 'FD' which indicates this push funds transfer is being conducted in order to facilitate a sales tax refund.

transactionAmount.description:
This field contains the transaction amount in the currency specified by the currency code in 'transactionCurrencyCode'. 
The amount of POS funds requested by the cardholder, expressed in the local currency in an original authorization or financial transaction. 
This field also contains the acquirer-assessed surcharge.            

Note: Transaction amount should be numeric. Refer to the Payouts Endpoint Guide on country-specific currency minor units. Refer to SMS POS Visa & Visa Electron
Technical Specifications - Appendix E Country and Currency codes for Card.

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JOD is 3, the amount is JOD 100.996.

feeProgramIndicator.description: Note: If present, a valid value is required. Spaces or special characters are not allowed.

businessApplicationId.description:
Business Application Identifier (BAI) identifies the type of program for which the payment is being sent, i.e. whether it is a funds disbursement, money transfer etc. It should be a valid value allowed by Visa and approved for the program during onboarding.

Valid BAI for Push to Cards:
- Money transfer: AA, PP, BI, FT, WT; 
- Non-money transfer: BB, BP, CP, FD, GD, GP, LO, MD, OG, PD, PS

transactionCurrencyCode.description:

When present, this field contains surcharge as assessed by the Originating Entity. Values in this field must be included in the transactionAmount and should be in the same currency and format as defined in the transactionAmount field.

Note: if card credential is provided in senderDetail, fund is debited by transactionAmount from sender's card; but credited by transactionAmount - surcharge to recipient's card
Technical Specifications - Appendix E Country and Currency codes for VDC.

transactionAmount.description:
This field contains the transaction amount in the currency specified by the currency code in 'transactionCurrencyCode'. 
The amount of POS funds requested by the cardholder, expressed in the local currency in an original authorization or financial transaction. 
This field also contains the acquirer-assessed surcharge.            

Note: Transaction amount should be numeric. Refer to the Payouts Endpoint Guide on country-specific currency minor units. Refer to SMS POS Visa & Visa Electron
Technical Specifications - Appendix E Country and Currency codes for Card.

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JOD is 3, the amount is JOD 100.996.

businessApplicationId.description:
Business Application Identifier (BAI) identifies the type of program for which the payment is being sent, i.e. whether it is a funds disbursement, money transfer etc. It should be a valid value allowed by Visa and approved for the program during onboarding.

Valid BAI for Push to Cards:
-	Money transfer: AA, PP, BI, FT, WT; 
-	Non-money transfer: BB, BP, CP, FD, GD, GP, LO, MD, OG, PD

destinationAmount.description:
The destination amount that will be deposited to the recipient account, expressed in the Recipient bank currency code provided in the original request. transactionAmount.description:
This field contains the transaction amount in the currency specified by the currency code in 'transactionCurrencyCode'. 
The amount of POS funds requested by the cardholder, expressed in the local currency in an original authorization or financial transaction. 
This field also contains the acquirer-assessed surcharge.            

Note: Transaction amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Payouts Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units. 

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JPY is 0. If the amount is JPY 10,000, then this field should populate “10000”.

ISO20022 field name: Instructed Amount

transactionCurrencyCode.description:

Format: 3-character ISO-4217 (Alpha-3) currency code

Example: "PHP"

enablerVerificationValue.description: Only applicable for pull reversal for CardsEnabler Verification Value (EVV) is a Visa assigned value that is used to identify enablers that participate in certain programs. The EVV is unique to the enabler.

retrievalReferenceNumber.description:
This is a unique identifier generated by Visa for a card transaction

The format is ydddhhnnnnnn
yddd - The first four digits must be a valid Julian date format, where the first digit = 0-9 (last digit of current year) and the next three digits = 001-366 (number of the day in the year). 
hh - can be the two digit hour in a 24 hour clock (00-23) during which the transaction is performed. 
nnnnnn - can be the systemsTraceAuditNumber or any 6 digit number

accountType.description:
Used to identify the account type of the recipientPrimaryAccountNumber in the request. Below are the possible values.

00-Not applicable

10-Saving account

20-Checking account

30-Credit card account

40-Universal account

Default is set to "00" if not provided.

Conditional

Note: Visa requires expiration date to be present in all OCTs destined to U.S. issuers
Format: YYYY-MM
Example: 2021-10

ISO20022 field name: N/A

motoECIIndicator.description:
Identifies the level of security used in an electronic commerce transaction over an open network (for example, the Internet) or the type of mail or telephone order. Acquirers supply indicator values, which Visa forwards in requests and advices to issuers that have successfully tested to receive them. The subfield is dropped if issuers have not successfully completed testing or choose not to receive it.
If not provided, Visa will default its value to 7 for US and 5 for rest of the world, when posConditionCode is 59

yddd - The first four digits must be a valid Julian date format, where the first digit = 0-9 (last digit of current year) and the next three digits = 001-366 (number of the day in the year). 
hh - can be the two digit hour in a 24 hour clock (00-23) during which the transaction is performed. 
nnnnnn - can be the systemsTraceAuditNumber or any 6 digit number

transactionAmount.description:

Note: Transaction amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Payouts Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units.

exemptionReasonCode.description:
One or more instances of reason codes that explain why an exemption was not honored.

Valid Values :
8A01 = Merchant not participating in Visa Delegated Authentication Program
8A02 = Issuer not participating in Visa Delegated Authentication Program
8A04 = Indeterminate or invalid issuer response
8A06 = Did not meet exemption criteria (Visa determined)
8A07 = VMID invalid for service
8A08 = CAVV invalid value
8A76 = Did not meet delegation criteria (Issuer supplied)
8473 = Cardholder has not trusted the merchant (issuer supplied)
8474 = Did not meet the exemption criteria (issuer supplied)
8976 = Did not meet exemption criteria (issuer supplied)

This field is present in API response only if any of the SCA exemptions were claimed and optionalResponseParameters field was set to include "RISKASSESSMENTDATA" as one of the comma separated values in the API request.

This field maps to ISO8583 Field 34, Dataset ID 4A- Tag 8C.

scpExemptionIndicator.description:
Secure Corporate Payment (SCP) Indicator.

Valid Values :
HONORED - Secure corporate payment exemption validated/honored
NOT_HONORED-Secure corporate payment exemption failed validation/not honored

This field is present in API response only if the exemption was claimed and optionalResponseParameters field was set to include "RISKASSESSMENTDATA" as one of the comma separated values in the API request.

This field maps to ISO8583 Field 34 – Dataset ID 4A -Tag 88.

traExemptionIndicator.description:

Valid Values :
HONORED - Transaction risk analysis exemption validated/honored
NOT_HONORED - Transaction risk analysis exemption failed validation/not honored

This field is present in API response only if the exemption was claimed and optionalResponseParameters field was set to include "RISKASSESSMENTDATA" as one of the comma separated values in the API request.

This field maps to ISO8583 Field 34 – Dataset ID 4A -Tag 89.

lowValueExemptionIndicator.description:
This field is present in API response only if the following conditions are met.

- optionalResponseParameters field was set to include "RISKASSESSMENTDATA" as one of the comma separated values in the API request.

- Low Value exemption was claimed in the acquirer request (OR) Issuer chooses to approve the transaction as the amount was below the issuer set low value and velocity counts limits

Valid Values :
HONORED - Low value exemption validated/honored
NOT_HONORED - Low value exemption failed validation/not honored

metadataVersion.description:
This is the version of the route definition recalled by VISA. 
It is in the format <major-version>.<minor-version>.<patch>.

* patch updates are documentation updates only and should not influence the processing of a payout transaction. Example: changes to the description of Purpose of Payment code.

* minor-version updates indicate backward compatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Example: addition of a new Purpose of Payment code.

* major-version updates indicate backward incompatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Such changes are usually regulatory in nature or due to partner migration on Visa's backend. Example: Purpose of Payment code changing from a "conditional"/ "recommended" to a "required" field.

metadataVersionDate.description: This was the expected go-live date of the recalled metadata version.

This is the version of the route definition recalled by VISA. 
It is in the format <major-version>.<minor-version>.<patch>.

* patch updates are documentation updates only and should not influence the processing of a payout transaction. Example: changes to the description of Purpose of Payment code.

* minor-version updates indicate backward compatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Example: addition of a new Purpose of Payment code.

* major-version updates indicate backward incompatible changes in the route validation rules on a payout transaction. Such changes are usually regulatory in nature or due to partner migration on Visa's backend. Example: Purpose of Payment code changing from a "conditional"/ "recommended" to a "required" field.

The amount of POS funds requested by the cardholder, expressed in the local currency in an original authorization or financial transaction. 
This field also contains the acquirer-assessed surcharge.            

Note: Transaction amount can have decimal point for currencies that allow it. Refer to the Payouts Endpoint Guide for Payout on country-specific currency minor units. 

Example: Currency exponent for USD is 2, the amount is $100.99. Currency exponent for JPY is 0. If the amount is JPY 10,000, then this field should populate “10000”.

ISO20022 field name: Instructed Amount

originalActionCode.description: Contains a code that provides the result of original payout request when current request is identified as duplicate of original and actionCode will be 94.

feeProgramIndicator.description: Note: If present, a valid value is required. Spaces or special characters are not allowed.

settlementCurrencyCode.description: Only applicable to push transferSettlement Currency code

systemTraceAuditNumber.description: This field contains a number generated by Visa that uniquely identifies a transaction and all message types. The trace number is a key data element used to match a response to its request or to match a message to others for a given transaction set

transactionCurrencyCode.description:
The 3-character ISO-4217 code in this field reflects the currency associated to the transaction amount. 

Format: 3-character ISO-4217 (Alpha-3) currency code

Example: "PHP"

enablerVerificationValue.description: Enabler Verification Value (EVV) is a Visa assigned value that is used to identify enablers that participate in certain programs. The EVV is unique to the enabler.

givPreviouslyUpdatedFlag.description: This field identifies the GivPreviouslyUpdatedFlag. Possible values are true or false

retrievalReferenceNumber.description:
This is a unique identifier generated by Visa for a card transaction

The format is ydddhhnnnnnn
yddd - The first four digits must be a valid Julian date format, where the first digit = 0-9 (last digit of current year) and the next three digits = 001-366 (number of the day in the year). 
hh - can be the two digit hour in a 24 hour clock (00-23) during which the transaction is performed. 
nnnnnn - can be the systemsTraceAuditNumber or any 6 digit number

Indicates funding status of the payout transaction.

FUNDED - Indicates that the payout is fully funded and the allocated funds are available for settlement.

NOT_FUNDED - Indicates that the payout has not yet been allocated any funds.

FUNDED_AGING - Indicates that the payout has been allocated funds but the funds are still in the required aging period.

destinationAmount.description:
The destination amount that will be deposited to the recipient account, expressed in the Recipient bank currency code provided in the original request. If the Originating Entity sends a payout in a currency that is not the same as the destination currency then Visa will perform FX conversion and calculate the amount to be deposited to the recipient bank account, and provide this information back to the Originating Entity.

RetrievalReferenceNumber-1.description:
This is a unique identifier generated by the Orignating Entity for a transaction and its one of the key fields for matching a transaction with the subsequent messages with in the transaction set example Notification, Returns, Cancel, Exception management via VD Portal for P2A and Reversals, Chargeback, Response, Advice for P2C. It is also used for duplicate validation check done by Visa.

The format is recommended to be ydddhhnnnnnn
yddd - The first four digits must be a valid Julian date format, where the first digit = 0-9 (last digit of current year) and the next three digits = 001-366 (number of the day in the year). 
hh - can be the two digit hour in a 24 hour clock (00-23) during which the transaction is performed. 
nnnnnn - can be the systemsTraceAuditNumber or any 6 digit number

status.description:
Status of the transaction
- PAYMENT_RECEIVED: Visa has acknowledged the payout instruction has been received. This event can be repeated when 'fundingStatus' or 'expectedPostingDate' fields change value
- AWAITING_INFORMATION: PSP is awaiting more information from Originating Entity before transaction can be processed
- PAYMENT_SENT: The payout has been submitted to the Network partner by PSP. This event can be repeated 'fundingStatus' or 'expectedPostingDate' fields change value
- PAYMENT_DELIVERED: The payout has been posted to the recipient's account. This status is only applicable for Wallet Payments
